newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh arrives in Manila today for a two-day state visit aimed at strengthening his country's relations with the Philippines, especially in the area of investments. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Zamboanga congressman Romeo Jalosjos is set to be arraigned today at the Makati Regional Trial Court on charges of statutory rape of a minor. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Water rates may be increased, without public hearings, according to the concession agreement signed between the government and the winners of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System privatisation deal. (MANILA TIMES)
- The two contracts for the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System are not yet a done deal, Public Works and Highways Secretary Virgilio Vigilar said. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said Philippine gross national product growth in 1996 may likely settle at 7.1 percent. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- Korean conglomerate Hanbo Group, burdened by cash problems and labour woes, has withdrawn from a proposed $1 billion ship building venture in the Philippines and instead decided to relocate in China. (BUSINESS WORLD)
- The Supreme Court ruled yesterday that foreign corporations can be subject to lawsuits in the Philippines.(THE PHILIPPINE STAR).
